correctness.rationale: The quoted uniqueness theorem for Lucas decompositions requires nonadjacent indices and excludes simultaneous indices 0 and 2. Each of the five displayed representations L_j+(23,25,27,29,31) with j=13+24m is legal, with lengths (4,3,4,2,3) for every nonnegative m. The exact recurrence pair L24=103682, L25=167761 reduces to (L0,L1) mod12, whence L_(13+24m)=5 mod12 by induction. This yields divisibility by 4,3,4,2,3 for the offsets and infinitely many strictly increasing starts. Fifteen starts were checked independently, with no claim about maximal possible run length.

originality.rationale: The complete accessible primary preprint by Lao et al. 2026 uses the same canonical Lucas decomposition but separately proves infinitely many single Lucas–Niven values in each arithmetic progression (Section 3) and five-term consecutive arithmetic runs for Zeckendorf–Niven numbers (Theorem 4.4). Those statements do not imply five simultaneous Lucas–Niven values with the claimed exact counts. The paper explicitly distinguishes the two count functions; the requested family is an original further consequence of its setup to the best of verified knowledge.

value.rationale: The motivating primary work treats both Lucas and Zeckendorf digital Niven properties yet gives an infinite five-term run only in the Zeckendorf setting. An infinite explicitly parameterized Lucas five-run with fixed canonical lengths and a uniform modular mechanism answers that natural missing companion problem; it is not a fixed numerical example or a claim of an unproved optimal length.
